summary: Petite Île au Marteau light in the Mingan Archipelago: lit 1915, rebuilt 1955 and 1976, staffed until 1987, now seasonal; reached by park trail or boat.

light.fog_signal: diaphone in the fog-alarm building from 1917 (LighthouseFriends; Quebec record); Marine annual report for 1918-19 lists a new fog-alarm plant at the island. Present fog signal not described in the sources read.
light.note: Coast Guard list: 'Seasonal'. Focal height and range are for the present light on the 1976 skeleton tower.

structures.type: wooden lighthouse with a square dwelling and square lantern on the hipped roof
structures.note: Demolished or removed in 1965 along with the old keeper's dwelling (LighthouseFriends; the Quebec record says the first light disappeared in 1965).

structures.type: wooden fog-alarm building (diaphone house; school in the workshop)
structures.note: Quebec record: the oldest structure still on the site. Fog alarm first dated 1917; Marine report for 1918-19 also lists a new plant that year.
Built 1954-55 (Quebec record); 38 feet (LighthouseFriends); built by Gulf Maritime Construction Ltd. Left standing when the light moved in 1976.
Carries the present light (LighthouseFriends; Coast Guard list gives a 25.3 m skeleton tower). Routes des phares describes the present light as the 12 m concrete tower of 1954; see notes_for_editor.

staffing.note: Complete automation dated 1976 (Quebec record) or early 1980s (LighthouseFriends). Last resident keepers left 1987 (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve. Boat trips run by a local operator (LighthouseFriends). Hiking trail to the light; grounds open, tower closed.

visit.note: Parks Canada hiking trail, lookout over the cliffs of Grosse île au Marteau; rockfall near the cliffs and slippery rocks at low tide (Parks Canada).

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (owner of the light, per LighthouseFriends); Parks Canada (Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve)

events.note: First light lit 11 August 1915; keeper Charles Boudreau hired (LighthouseFriends).
New aid erected by the Department: lighthouse, dwelling and oil shed; expenditure $3,573 (Marine report 1915-16; LighthouseFriends names the contractor S. Menier).
Fog-alarm building added with a diaphone (LighthouseFriends; the Quebec record says the fog-alarm building followed in 1917).
The Marine report for fiscal 1918-19 says new fog-alarm plants were established that year, at Ile au Marteau among others. Conflicts with 1917.
Two oil storage tanks installed at Isle au Marteau (Marine report for fiscal 1922-23).
Octagonal reinforced-concrete tower, 12 m (Quebec record: 1954-55; LighthouseFriends: 1955).
Old keeper's dwelling and the first light demolished; new keeper's dwelling built; two generators installed in the fog-alarm building.
Light moved to a new steel skeleton tower; the concrete tower was left standing (LighthouseFriends).
Quebec record: complete automation of the light sector in 1976. LighthouseFriends dates automation to the early 1980s.
Last resident keepers leave the island (LighthouseFriends).
Federal renovation of the station's buildings, including the interior of the newer keeper's dwelling and the foghorn building; completion announced October 2010.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikidata gives 1910 for the tower. LighthouseFriends and the Quebec record date the first light to 1915 and the present tower to 1955 and 1976. The 1910 date has no support in the sources read.
The Coast Guard list marks the light 'Seasonal', so it is lit for part of the year rather than continuously. LighthouseFriends does not say the light is out of service.

notes_for_editor: 1) Fog-alarm year: 1917 (LighthouseFriends; Quebec record) against 'new fog-alarm plants established' at Ile au Marteau in the fiscal 1918-19 report. The story gives both and does not choose. 2) Present tower: the Coast Guard list (25.3 m skeleton tower, seasonal) and LighthouseFriends (steel skeleton tower erected 1976) agree; Routes des phares says the present light is the 12 m concrete tower of 1954, which is probably the older tower. The 1910 date and 25.3 m height in the station record match only the Coast Guard list's skeleton tower. 3) Automation: complete in 1976 (Quebec record) against the early 1980s (LighthouseFriends). The story gives both. 4) Fiscal 1915-16 cost: the $3,573 figure appears in the Marine report's works table for 'Ile au Marteau' (scan p.56, printed p.49, under 'QUEBEC. New Aids to Navigation') and in LighthouseFriends (with S. Menier named). The row was matched by position in the OCR block sequence and then checked against the page image on 2026-10-28: the contractor column reads S. Menier, the expenditure 3,573.00, and the works line begins 'Erection lighthouse, dwelling, oil'. The OCR text does not contain 'Menier'; that name comes from the image and from LighthouseFriends. 5) Keeper roster: LighthouseFriends gives five names in one 'Keepers' line; it does not say who was head keeper and who was assistant. The schoolteachers (1934 to 1949) are not named in any source read. 6) The 1952 house: Quebec record says assistant keeper; LighthouseFriends says head keeper. Not reconciled. 7) Marine reports for fiscal 1920-21 list 'He au Marteau' with 'Repairs to dwelling and tower' and 'Repairs to fog alarm building and coal shed'. The OCR table does not show which item belongs to which station, so these are not used in the story. 8) The Marine reports in the corpus end in 1923-24; the 1930s to 1970s facts come from the Quebec record, LighthouseFriends and the Coast Guard list only. 9) Parks Canada's 'prevented many shipwreck' statement is promotional and names no wreck; it is attributed, not treated as a record of wrecks. 10) The Quebec sector record gives the 1941 Parks Canada context and the fog building as the oldest structure; it does not name any keeper. 11) The 1918-19 'He au Marteau' is the OCR reading of 'Ile au Marteau' in narrative text under QUEBEC AGENCY (scan p.97, printed p.90); it was read from the OCR text, not the image. The 1922-23 tanks (scan p.107, printed p.100) are likewise from the narrative OCR.
